newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech stocks move sharply lower led by CEZ.
newsitem.headline: Czech stocks move sharply lower led by CEZ.

text.p: The main Czech share indices fell on Wednesday with major issues, especially power utility CEZ, applying most of the downward pressure.
The PX50 lost 7.5 points, 1.5 percent, to 480.7 while the high cap dominated RPIX fell 21.7 points, more than two percent, to 972.7.

CEZ crashed through its previous 12-month low of 935 crowns per share, losing 37 crowns, or three percent, to 908. CEZ has traditionally performed worse than other major issues because of the politically sensitive problem of lifting electricty price regulation.

But Michael Gartner, an equities analyst specialising in the Czech energy sector, said the government would have to tackle the problem sooner or later adding that CEZ represented a good cheap buy at current prices for investors prepared to wait into the long term before realising significant gains.
"People are waiting to see some really quick action from the government about deregulation. But it is going to happen. People putting money in are taking a long term view," he said.
On Friday, CEZ is due to release nine month finacial results.

Elsewhere, all the highly capitalised shares fell. Komercni Banka was the biggest points decliner, losing 69 crowns to 1,931. Komercni was closely followed by the bourse's most heavily weighted issue, SPT Telecom, which dropped 53 crowns 2,732.
Tuesday's sharpest faller, Ceska Sporitelna, fell by four crowns to 295.
